prompt: How should invoice export run: a synchronous CSV download, or a background job that emails a download link? Get the team to decide.

assertions.text: Runs project-discovery first. Starts Team Secretary with an active meeting record when Agent Teams are available; otherwise uses subagent mode and marks capture NOT VERIFIED.
assertions.evidence_quote: **Discovery gate not run:** I didn't run `/project-discovery`, and there is no `docs/agent-ops/READINESS_MATRIX.md` yet.

judge.reason: The assertion requires project-discovery to run first. The agent says it did not run project-discovery, and its tool calls confirm this: the only skill invoked was team-debate. It did use subagent mode and mark capture NOT VERIFIED, but because the first requirement is missing, the assertion fails.

assertions.text: Collects independent first proposals before peers see each other's views.
assertions.evidence_quote: You are a VOTER in an Orcasus team debate (subagent mode; independent first proposal — you see no peer output). Read-only.

judge.reason: The agent asked four voter subagents for first proposals, and each was told it would see no peer output. Only after all four round-1 proposals were in did it use SendMessage to share summaries of the other voters' proposals for the rebuttal round. The ballots file also says "every voter got the same independent brief."

assertions.text: Requires peer challenge, rebuttal and a Devil's Advocate alternative.
assertions.evidence_quote: - **Performance reviewer → devil's advocate:** the "maps and stringifies everything" problem is in the existing JSON route, not in a streamed export. A row cap does not fix a slow link.

judge.reason: The evidence shows all three parts. A Devil's Advocate voter put forward its own alternative (A+, which it called "C" in round 1) when the other three voters chose A. There was a rebuttal round, sent to each voter through SendMessage. During that round the voters challenged each other directly, recorded as named pairs such as architect→performance and performance→devil's advocate. The Devil's Advocate's alternative then won the final vote.

assertions.text: Scores with an explicit weighted matrix and collects explicit FINAL_BALLOT messages; never infers votes from silence.
assertions.evidence_quote: **Format gap:** the devil's advocate's final ballot leaves out the `voter` and `reason` fields. The voter's identity comes from the agent it was sent to. Its stated reason is in its rebuttal: without the cap, A has no defined behaviour when the 40k assumption fails. The vote was explicitly cast, not inferred.

judge.reason: The ballots file sets out explicit weights (fit 20, ux 15, sec 20, complexity 15, perf 20, cost 10) and gives per-voter weighted matrix rows for both rounds. It also includes verbatim FINAL_BALLOT blocks from all four voters in both rounds. One ballot was incomplete. The agent flagged the gap and stated that the vote was explicitly cast, not inferred. No vote was taken from silence.

assertions.text: Records the decision state, dissent and revisit triggers in an ADR.
assertions.evidence_quote: - Status: **ESCALATE**. The team recommends A+ and the product owner decides. The owner said on 2026-10-25: "I decide after the ADR."

judge.reason: ADR-0002 records all three items. The decision state is marked "Status: ESCALATE". Dissent appears in a section called "Dissent and unresolved disagreement" that covers the round-1 dissent and the points still contested. Revisit triggers have their own "Revisit triggers" section with specific conditions.
